classification.difficultyReason: Use parallel sides to establish AAS congruence and transfer lengths through rectangles, then choose an area decomposition to recover the parallelogram's area. Earlier parts scaffold the lengths and one component area, but the final subtraction strategy must be identified.

spec.description: Complete parallelogram and perpendicular scaffold, reconstructed with coordinates satisfying all supplied lengths. Ordinary source blue lines become black; no shading is required.
spec.mathematics: A=(0,12), B=(7,6), C=(12,10), D=(5,16); P=(0,0), Q=(5,0), R=(7,0), S=(12,0), X=(5,12), Y=(12,6). AP, DQ, BR and CS are perpendicular to PS; AX and BY are horizontal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source vertex labels and right-angle markers are shown; derived lengths remain hidden.

answer.worked:
In triangles $ADX$ and $BCY$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AXD&=\angle BYC=90^\circ,\\\angle ADX&=\angle BCY,\\AD&=BC.\end{align*}$$
The second equality holds because $AD\parallel BC$ and $DX\parallel CY$. The side equality follows from opposite sides of a parallelogram. Therefore $\triangle ADX\equiv\triangle BCY$ by AAS.

answer.short: $BY=AX=PQ=5$, using matching sides and opposite sides of rectangle $AXQP$.
answer.worked: $AXQP$ is a rectangle, so $AX=PQ=5$. Matching sides of the congruent triangles in part a give $BY=AX$. Hence $BY=5$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the length of the interval $BR$.

answer.worked:
$BYRS$ is a rectangle, so $RS=BY=5$. The parallel sides of trapezium $BRSC$ are $BR$ and $CS$.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(BRSC)&=\frac12(BR+CS)RS\\\operatorname{area}(BRSC)&=\frac12(6+10)(5)\\\operatorname{area}(BRSC)&=40\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find the area of the parallelogram $ABCD$.

answer.short:
$58$ square units.

Subtract the two regions below $AB$ and $BC$ from the region beneath $AD$ and $DC$.
answer.worked:
$PR=PQ+QR=7$, $QS=QR+RS=7$, and $RS=5$.
Split the region beneath $AD$ and $DC$ at $DQ$, then subtract the regions beneath $AB$ and $BC$:
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(PADQ)&=\frac12(12+16)(5)=70,\\\operatorname{area}(QDCS)&=\frac12(16+10)(7)=91,\\\operatorname{area}(PABR)&=\frac12(12+6)(7)=63.\end{align*}$$
Part d gives $\operatorname{area}(BRSC)=40$. Therefore
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{area}(ABCD)&=70+91-63-40\\\operatorname{area}(ABCD)&=58\text{ square units}.\end{align*}$$
